name: Ahasuerus
description: Emperor Xerxes I, living at the time of Exile and Return

points: In the reign of Ahasuerus and later Artaxerxes, the adversaries write accusations against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem.

note.label: Ezra 4: The Adversaries Halt the Building

points: Ahasuerus reigned from India unto Ethiopia over 127 provinces, and the power of Persia and Media stood before him. This is the same land where Mordecai and Hadassah were, which we are about to celebrate at Purim.
In the days of Ahasuerus, who reigned from India even unto Ethiopia over a hundred and twenty seven provinces, the king sat on the throne of his kingdom in Shushan the palace.

note.label: Esther 1: Vashti Refuses the King and the Law of Order in the House

points: After the wrath of king Ahasuerus was appeased he remembered Vashti and what she had done and what was decreed against her. His servants counsel that fair young virgins be sought for the king in every province and gathered to Shushan the palace under the custody of the keeper of the women.

note.label: Esther 2: Esther Made Queen and Mordecai Uncovers the Plot

points: Two of the king's chamberlains, of those which kept the door, were wroth, and sought to lay hand on the king Ahasuerus. And the thing was known to Mordecai, who told it unto Esther the queen; and Esther certified the king thereof in Mordecai's name. Inquisition was made; both were hanged on a tree; and it was written in the book of the chronicles before the king. Mordecai saved the king's life, and it went on record.

note.label: Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred We Never Learned

points: In those days, while Mordecai sat in the king's gate, two of the king's chamberlains that kept the door were wroth and sought to lay hands on king Ahasuerus, plotting a coup against him.

note.label: Esther 2: Esther Made Queen and Mordecai Uncovers the Plot

points: After these things did king Ahasuerus promote Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite. Sound familiar? This is a descendant of the same Agag that Samuel hewed in pieces. Haman is an Amalekite, an Edomite, and the king set his seat above all the princes: the right hand of the king over Persia.

note.label: Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred We Never Learned

points: And he thought scorn to lay hands on Mordecai alone: Haman sought to destroy all the Jews that were throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus, for what one Jew would not do. Why all of them? Remember what king Saul was sent to do to Amalek. Haman's people kept the records; he knew Mordecai's line, the line of Kish, was the line sent to destroy his forefathers. Esau forgave Jacob, but his children hold the grudge from generation to generation. They do not forget; we do.

note.label: Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred We Never Learned

points: Haman sought to destroy all the Jews throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus, the people of Mordecai, not one man only. Because Mordecai would not bow, Edom's hatred sought a death sentence for the entire nation, seeking to erase us out of history.

note.label: Esther 3: Haman the Agagite and the Decree to Destroy the Jews

points: Mardocheus the Jew was next unto king Ahasuerus, great among the Jews and accepted of the multitude of his brethren, seeking the wealth of his people and speaking peace to all his seed.

note.label: Esther 10: Mardocheus Exalted and the Dream Interpreted

points: In the first year of Darius the son of Ahasuerus, of the seed of the Medes, made king over the realm of the Chaldeans, Daniel understood by the books the seventy years of the desolations of Jerusalem spoken to Jeremiah.
